digest.component_or_area: code health metrics and module-size gate
propositions: 40+ src/rebar Python files exceed 700 LOC with 7 files at or near the 800-line hard cap; pass1.py and push.py are each at 800 LOC and require extraction to reduce headroom exhaustion.

Module-level monkeypatching of push._git across 25 test sites creates a binding-time hazard when extracted functions call _git; the fix is late-binding resolution via a core parameter pattern, following _ref_lock_push.py precedent.

_submit_ctx in pass1.py must move to generation.py (not to the new container_stage module) because it launches pool workers that read generation's _CANCEL_SCOPE ContextVar via copy_context(), and leaving it in pass1 would create a cycle.

A near-cap warning already exists (module_size_distribution.near_cap_count), computed since scc was installed and the adapter bug c5b3-1b8a-08dd-40af was fixed, but surfacing it requires appending a non-blocking pass to the CI Module-size gate step in .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml.

The extraction of pass1.py (800→534 LOC) separates container pairing logic into container_stage.py (296 LOC) while preserving all pass1 re-exports so orchestrator.py and provider_parity.py imports remain byte-unchanged.

The extraction of push.py (800→524 LOC) separates the 8-function recovery cluster into push_recovery.py (366 LOC) using core-parameter late binding to preserve monkeypatch sites, with delegating shims in push.py for backward-compatible direct test calls.
